exposure: Sucrose-induced metabolic syndrome in Wistar rat progenitors
outcome: Absence of Xiphoid and Sterne brae
cohort: The study included Wistar rat fetuses from progenitors, some of whom developed metabolic syndrome after being supplied with 35% sucrose from the intrauterine stage up to eighteen weeks of age.
finding: The metabolic syndrome in progenitors significantly decreased fetal weight, caused hematoma, and led to developmental delays in bone tissue, specifically the absence of Xiphoid and Sterne brae, suggesting a morphological impact on the conception product.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome; significant decrease in fetuses' weight observed in the metabolic syndrome group.
gest_age: Fetuses were studied at day twenty of gestation.
